evals.prompt: Show me my unread Outlook inbox messages from this morning.
evals.expected_output: Checks Microsoft Graph login status first, then lists unread inbox messages bounded to this morning with the mgraphctl CLI.

assertions.name: checks-status-first
assertions.description: The response runs the mgraphctl status check before any mailbox command.

assertions.name: uses-mail-list-unread
assertions.description: The response uses `mail list --unread`, not a raw `api` call.

assertions.name: bounds-the-morning
assertions.description: The response passes an --after (and optionally --before) bound carrying a time of day, rather than filtering the whole day's mail by eye.

evals.prompt: Find every email from anyone at example.com since 1 July, and tell me whether the results were cut short by the pagination cap.
evals.expected_output: Runs a windowed mail search with --all and --json, then answers the truncation question from the envelope's truncated and cap fields rather than guessing.

assertions.name: uses-json-envelope
assertions.description: The response passes --json and reads `truncated` and `cap` from the envelope to answer whether results were cut short.

assertions.name: does-not-equate-count-with-completeness
assertions.description: The response does not conclude the results are complete merely because fewer items came back than the limit.

evals.prompt: Show me everything said in my Teams chat with a teammate since last Monday, going past the first page if needed.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the chat, then reads its messages with a --after bound and --all so paging continues past the first page.

assertions.name: uses-chats-messages-window
assertions.description: The response uses `chats messages` with --after (and --all where more than one page is wanted).

assertions.name: does-not-page-by-hand
assertions.description: The response does not try to follow @odata.nextLink itself through the raw `api` command.

evals.prompt: Which of my Teams chats have had a message in the last three days?
evals.expected_output: Uses `chats list --since` so paging stops at the boundary, rather than listing every chat and filtering the output by eye.

assertions.name: uses-chats-list-since
assertions.description: The response uses `chats list --since` with a relative or absolute bound.

assertions.name: does-not-filter-by-eye
assertions.description: The response does not list all chats unbounded and then discard the old ones itself.

evals.prompt: Search Teams for mentions of 'budget review' and then read what was said around any channel hit.
evals.expected_output: Searches chat and channel messages, then follows a channel hit into `teams channel messages` using the hit's teamId and channelId, with a time window around it.

assertions.name: searches-then-follows-up
assertions.description: The response runs `chats search` and then reads the surrounding messages for at least one hit.

assertions.name: uses-structured-hit-ids
assertions.description: The response follows a channel hit using its teamId and channelId fields rather than parsing the `where` string apart.

assertions.name: windows-the-follow-up
assertions.description: The follow-up read passes --after/--before around the hit's timestamp instead of fetching the whole channel.

evals.prompt: Summarise yesterday's standup meeting and list the action items.
evals.expected_output: Finds the meeting, fetches its transcript with --speakers so each speaker's turns read as one block, and summarises from that.

assertions.name: finds-the-meeting-first
assertions.description: The response locates the meeting and its transcript id before fetching content.

assertions.name: uses-speaker-turns
assertions.description: The response fetches the transcript with --speakers rather than reading one line per cue.

evals.prompt: What's on my calendar between 9am and noon tomorrow?
evals.expected_output: Lists calendar events for that window with explicit --start/--end (or --after/--before) bounds carrying a time of day.

assertions.name: uses-calendar-list-window
assertions.description: The response uses `calendar list` with bounds that carry a time of day, not just a date.

evals.prompt: Post 'Sprint planning at 2pm tomorrow' to the announcements channel in the Engineering team.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the team and channel by name, previews the send with --dry-run, and asks before actually posting.

assertions.name: dry-runs-before-writing
assertions.description: The response previews the write with --dry-run and confirms before sending.

assertions.name: uses-channel-send
assertions.description: The response uses `teams channel send` with the team and channel named.

evals.prompt: Send a message on Slack to the project channel.
evals.expected_output: Declines to use this skill: Slack is not a Microsoft 365 service and mgraphctl cannot reach it.

assertions.name: does-not-trigger
assertions.description: The response does not invoke the mgraphctl skill or any of its commands.

evals.prompt: I'm not signed in to anything yet — what do I need to do before you can read my mail?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a data command never opens a browser, and points at the login command, without attempting a data read first.

assertions.name: explains-login
assertions.description: The response names the login command rather than running a data command and reporting its error.
